# CrowdStrike FDR Receiver

This receiver ingests CrowdStrike Falcon Data Replicator (FDR) batches announced on the CrowdStrike-provided SQS queue and stored in the CrowdStrike-provided S3 bucket.

This receiver ingests [CrowdStrike Falcon Data Replicator (FDR)](https://www.crowdstrike.com/resources/data-sheets/falcon-data-replicator/) data.
FDR writes batches of gzipped, newline-delimited JSON files to a CrowdStrike-owned S3 bucket and publishes one notification per batch on a CrowdStrike-owned SQS queue.
The receiver long-polls that queue, waits for the batch `_SUCCESS` marker, downloads and decompresses every file in the batch, and decodes its newline-delimited JSON events.

Each event becomes one log record with the event as a map body. The log timestamp is taken from the field the feed uses: `timestamp` (sensor events, epoch milliseconds), `UTCTimestamp` (external events, epoch milliseconds), `Time` (aidmaster, epoch seconds), `_time` (managedassets, notmanaged, appinfo, userinfo, epoch seconds) or `modified_time` (zero trust host assessment, RFC 3339). Records without any of these keep a zero timestamp.

Every emitted resource carries `aws.s3.bucket` and `aws.s3.key`. Use the key prefix (`data/`, `fdrv2/aidmaster/`, `fdrv2/managedassets/`, ...) to route sensor events and inventory feeds downstream.

## Configuration

| Name | Description | Default | Required |
|:-----|:------------|:--------|:---------|
| `queue_url` | URL of the FDR SQS queue shown on the CrowdStrike API clients page. | | Yes |
| `region` | AWS region of the queue and bucket. | | Yes |
| `access_key_id` | FDR access key ID issued by CrowdStrike. | | No |
| `secret_access_key` | FDR secret access key issued by CrowdStrike. | | No |
| `visibility_timeout` | How long a batch notification stays hidden while it is ingested. A batch that is not ingested within this time is retried. | `5m` | No |
| `max_number_of_messages` | Batch notifications fetched per poll (1-10). | `10` | No |

When `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key` are empty the receiver uses the default AWS credential chain (environment, shared config, instance role).

## Delivery semantics

A batch notification is deleted from the queue only after every file in it has been decoded and accepted by the pipeline.
If the `_SUCCESS` marker is missing, a download fails, or the pipeline rejects the data, the notification becomes visible again after `visibility_timeout` and the whole batch is retried, so files that were already delivered can be duplicated.
Messages that are not FDR batch notifications are discarded.

## Example

```yaml
receivers:
  crowdstrike_fdr:
    queue_url: https://sqs.us-west-1.amazonaws.com/<account>/cs-prod-cannonball-<queue>
    region: us-west-1
    access_key_id: ${env:FDR_ACCESS_KEY_ID}
    secret_access_key: ${env:FDR_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY}

service:
  pipelines:
    logs:
      receivers: [crowdstrike_fdr]
      exporters: [debug]
```
